caption:
Your proposal prompt used to land. Now the output is flabbier and you can't say why.

Nothing changed on your side. The model did. OpenAI removed the GPT-5.1 models from ChatGPT in March 2026 and moved existing conversations onto newer ones; GPT-4.5 and o3 were each retired after a published sunset period. Prompts you tuned against an older model don't get a migration notice.

So keep the five prompts that make you money in one plain text file — proposal, follow-up, scope change, invoice chase, case study — with one good output saved next to each. That saved output is the benchmark. Without it you're arguing with your memory.

Then run slide 4 whenever your default model shifts. It compares old output to new, names what drifted, and rewrites the prompt to get the old quality back.

What it can't do: bring back a retired model. Sometimes the honest answer is that the prompt needs rebuilding.

Save this. Which of your five prompts would you notice breaking first?

body.t: OpenAI removed the GPT-5.1 models from ChatGPT in March 2026 and carried old chats onto newer ones. GPT-4.5 and o3 followed, each with a sunset period.
Your saved prompts get no notice.
Proposal, follow-up, scope change, invoice chase, case study. Plain text, not buried in chat history.
Keep one good output saved beside each.

slides.headline: Run the regression test.
slides.sub: Ten minutes, once, whenever your model changes under you.
slides.label: COPY THIS PROMPT
slides.code:
Here is a prompt I have used for a year
and the output I want back.
[paste prompt]
[paste last good output]
Run the prompt now, then compare:
what's missing, what's worse, what drifted
in tone. Rewrite the prompt so today's
model returns the old result. Show the
differences in plain language.

slides.headline: A prompt can't undo a retirement.

body.t: You can't get a removed model back. And swaps change tone more quietly than accuracy, so
judge against your last good deliverable, not your memory.

slides.headline: The system
items: Five money prompts in one file
Save one good output per prompt
Re-run both when the model shifts
Fix the prompt, not the output
